notes.title: Second Song
notes.originalTitle: Second Song
notes.subtitle: A few immediate reactions to Neil Young's new studio album
notes.text:
Lofi revisits his relationship with Neil Young through Second Song. An early listen to the title track left him unconvinced, but hearing it within the album changed his response. He hears a reflective record in which plainspoken songwriting and social commitment reinforce one another.

The essay considers why familiar musical gestures can acquire new weight late in an artist's life, and why Young's directness remains part of his appeal.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Five-Year Anniversary Show
notes.originalTitle: Five-Year Anniversary Show
notes.subtitle: Music as spirituality, community as the point — and this week, a loud, rocking set to prove it.
notes.text:
Marking five years of the show, Lofi reflects on radio as a weekly musical journal and on the community formed around it. He thanks Shady Pines and other listeners and musicians for giving the practice meaning.

The accompanying broadcast takes a louder direction, with longstanding favorites and newer records. Its introduction connects that rock set with his broader view of music as a personal and shared spiritual practice.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Here Comes the Sun
notes.originalTitle: Here Comes the Sun
notes.subtitle: A rerun from 2023, inspired by a Pickathon morning and Richie Havens.
notes.text:
Lofi returns to a 2023 show recorded before his first Pickathon DJ appearance. He traces the project from homemade basement broadcasts to finding Shady Pines Radio through a neighborhood flyer.

A festival-morning encounter with Richie Havens' version of Here Comes the Sun becomes the link between listening and wanting to help create that atmosphere himself. The original includes the rerun's recording, playlist and memories of joining a community through music.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Pickathon Memories No. 5: Michael Hurley
notes.originalTitle: Pickathon Memories at the Pendarvis Farm
notes.subtitle: No. 5 — Michael Hurley at the Woods Stage, 2010
notes.text:
The fifth Pickathon memory returns to Michael Hurley's Sunday-morning Woods Stage set in 2010. Lofi remembers the canopy, morning light and unhurried feeling of being fully settled into the festival. Hurley's songs seemed particularly at home there.

The piece connects that performance with smaller Portland shows and with the community that continues to celebrate Hurley's music and artwork. A recording of the set accompanies the original article.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Pickathon Memories No. 4: Ty Segall & the Rolin Stons
notes.originalTitle: Pickathon Memories at the Pendarvis Farm
notes.subtitle: No. 4 — Ty Segall and the Rolin Stons (aka Wand), 2015
notes.text:
A memory of Ty Segall's 2015 Galaxy Barn performance with the Rolin Stons, the musicians from Wand. Lofi recalls a packed barn, garage-rock songs, a Velvet Underground cover and Rolling Stones riffs pushed into unruly experiments.

The appeal is the sense of musicians taking risks together. The original links to footage from their Woods Stage performance, while the barn set survives primarily in memory.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Pickathon Memories No. 3: Kikagaku Moyo
notes.originalTitle: Pickathon Memories at the Pendarvis Farm
notes.subtitle: No. 3 - Kikagaku Moyo’s Legendary Set at the Starlight Stage, 2018
notes.text:
Lofi remembers discovering Kikagaku Moyo at Pickathon's Starlight Stage in 2018. Knowing little about the band beforehand, he was drawn into its hypnotic rhythms and guitar playing beneath the festival's fabric canopy, with Mount Hood and the night sky beyond.

The memory becomes an argument for leaving room for unexpected discoveries at festivals. Later performances were memorable too, but this first encounter retained a particular atmosphere.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Pickathon Memories No. 2: Justin Townes Earle
notes.originalTitle: Pickathon Memories at the Pendarvis Farm
notes.subtitle: No. 2 — Justin Townes Earle, a hot summer day in the Galaxy Barn
notes.text:
This Pickathon memory centers on Justin Townes Earle's 2009 performance in a very hot Galaxy Barn. Lofi recalls his presence as a solo performer, the closing song and a brief conversation after the set.

Reading Earle's biography later gave the experience a different emotional context. The article reflects on music, family and the weight that a remembered performance can acquire over time, with links to recordings from the festival.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Pickathon Memories No. 1: Gospel, Gravel & Family Tapes
notes.originalTitle: Pickathon Memories at the Pendarvis Farm
notes.subtitle: First of Many — Gospel, Gravel and Give Me Just a Little More Time
notes.text:
The Pickathon series opens with a 2025 Woods Stage DJ set between Jimetta Rose and Dylan Earl. Lofi recalls following the gospel performance with a Chairmen of the Board record that carried a family connection: his grandfather's radio mixtapes, later played by his mother.

The piece explains how a DJ set can connect personal memory with the mood of a shared space, moving between gospel, soul and folk while keeping the afternoon's feeling intact.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Do You Want It Darker
notes.originalTitle: Do You Want It Darker
notes.subtitle: Late recognition, and finding clarity in heavy times
notes.text:
A return to Leonard Cohen's Do You Want It Darker changes Lofi's previously distant appreciation of the songwriter. He hears an album that addresses mortality and uncertainty with patience, clarity and emotional honesty.

The essay places that listening experience within a difficult week, finding solidarity in Cohen's music. Its focus is the personal shift from admiring a handful of songs to feeling a deeper connection with an artist's work.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Bread of Angels and the Places We Come From
notes.originalTitle: Bread of Angels and the Places We Come From
notes.subtitle: On Patti Smith, proximity, and choosing art over expectation
notes.text:
Reading Patti Smith's Bread of Angels prompts Lofi to revisit growing up in St. Clair Shores, where Smith also lived, and buying Horses as a teenager. A brief everyday sighting made a distant artistic figure feel human and close to home.

The essay reflects on Smith's commitment to art, love and improvisation, and on how places and ordinary encounters can shape a listener's understanding of an artist.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Music Person
notes.originalTitle: Music Person
notes.subtitle: So… what does The Search for Skip James actually mean?
notes.text:
Lofi explains The Search for Skip James as a way of connecting older records, overlooked artists and personal stories with the present. Each show starts with records that are calling to him, then follows a thread across styles and eras.

He describes being a musician and collector alongside everyday work and family life. Physical records, imperfect sound and changing taste are part of the practice; sharing music and meeting other listeners are its community dimension.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: The Search for Skip James
notes.originalTitle: The Search for Skip James
notes.subtitle: Deep Grooves & Seasonal Drones
notes.text:
Notes for a dark, rhythm-driven November set, prompted in part by seeing Motrik's Earth release show. Lofi follows the seasonal atmosphere into drones, deep grooves and more abrasive sounds.

The original includes the full playlist, bringing together Motrik, Swell Maps, John Cale and Terry Riley, the Wipers, Can, Faust and other artists. This is the introductory writing attached to the radio episode from the link shared for the website.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Geese – Getting Killed
notes.originalTitle: Geese – Getting Killed
notes.subtitle: Immediate thoughts
notes.text:
An immediate response to Geese's Getting Killed, focused on Cameron Winter's distinctive voice and the band's rough, dynamic rock sound. Lofi hears connections with earlier rock groups while finding the record responsive to the anxiety of its own moment.

The note presents his listening impressions rather than a formal review, tracing the energy and repeated-listening appeal that have kept the album in rotation.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: THE SEARCH FOR SKIP JAMES ARCHIVE
notes.originalTitle: THE SEARCH FOR SKIP JAMES ARCHIVE
notes.subtitle: Mixtape Madness & 420 Easter Vibes
notes.text:
Notes for a radio set broadcast on Easter Sunday and April 20. Lofi approaches the show as a mixtape, concentrating on the flow between very different records rather than a single genre.

The original includes the recording and full tracklist, moving through artists such as Desmond Dekker, Michael Hurley, Richie Havens, Cindy Lee, Laraaji and Moondog. The emphasis is on surprising transitions and the pleasure of following one song into another.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Doom Town: Radio Show Archive
notes.originalTitle: Doom Town: Radio Show Archive
notes.subtitle: April 2025
notes.text:
A record-store conversation and the Wipers' Over the Edge provide the starting point for Doom Town. Lofi connects the set's uneasy atmosphere with the uncertainty surrounding everyday life and work.

He also announces that radio archives will be shared through Substack and acknowledges the response to his Michael Hurley tribute. The original contains the full playlist, with punk, experimental rock and other records chosen to accompany a heavy mood.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Snock Forever: A Tribute to Michael Hurley
notes.originalTitle: Snock Forever: A Tribute to Michael Hurley
notes.subtitle: by DJ Lofi | Jason Bimberg
notes.text:
A personal tribute to Michael Hurley, built from nearly two decades of encounters around Portland. Lofi recalls first hearing Werewolf, buying Armchair Boogie after a deli performance and seeing Hurley play in small venues, parks and record shops.

The essay celebrates his distinctive songs, humor and unhurried approach. It includes a tribute broadcast and detailed notes on the selected recordings, connecting particular records with memories of the person who made them.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Words: Post Radio Show Blog
notes.originalTitle: Words: Post Radio Show Blog
notes.subtitle: The Power of Words, Song, and Story
notes.text:
Lofi considers how songs move from a writer's personal experience into the lives of listeners. Meaning changes as a song is performed, remembered and heard in new circumstances.

The radio set follows that idea through lyricists and songwriters including Bob Dylan, David Berman, Joni Mitchell, Townes Van Zandt and others. The original pairs the playlist with individual listening notes about humor, melancholy, storytelling and the emotional reach of words set to music.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Post-Radio Show Blog: The Search for Skip James
notes.originalTitle: Post-Radio Show Blog: The Search for Skip James
notes.subtitle: Guitar, Influence, and the Journey
notes.text:
A two-part guitar theme leads Lofi back to formative listening experiences, early lessons in Metro Detroit and the blues players behind much of the rock music he loves. He describes an approach centered on feeling, storytelling and imperfect performances.

The essay also explains his effort to add more conversation and narrative to the radio show. Two setlists connect surf, folk, blues and rock guitar, with a link to the archived broadcasts.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: A High Note to Start the Year
notes.originalTitle: A High Note to Start the Year
notes.subtitle: First Show of 2025: Searching for Skip James…
notes.text:
The first post of 2025 begins with a New Year's Eve show featuring Jenny Don't & the Spurs and White Lightning Co. Lofi carries that sense of musical community into a new radio set assembled from a fresh stack of records.

The article includes track-by-track reflections, gratitude for Portland's musicians and record shops, and his response to the Bob Dylan film A Complete Unknown. It documents what he was listening to at the start of that year.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Post Radio Blog: My Favorite Albums of 2024
notes.originalTitle: Post Radio Blog: My Favorite Albums of 2024
notes.text:
A personal account of the records that accompanied Lofi through 2024, rather than an attempt at a definitive ranking. Rosali's Bite Down leads the selection, alongside music by the Cosmic Tones Research Trio, David Nance, Adrianne Lenker, Gillian Welch and David Rawlings, Jim White and Marisa Anderson, Cindy Lee, Nick Cave and Myriam Gendron.

The accompanying notes connect repeated listening with live performances, friends' recommendations and the moods that made these albums matter to him.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Set and Setting: Warming Up with Music from Around the World
notes.originalTitle: Set and Setting: Warming Up with Music from Around the World
notes.text:
With his furnace out during winter, Lofi builds a radio set around the relationship between mindset, surroundings and music. Records from Jamaica and Africa become a way to change the atmosphere of a cold December day.

Joe Boyd's The Roots of Rhythm Remain also informs the selection. The original includes listening notes on reggae, ska, Afrobeat and Ethiopian music, tracing warmth and cultural connections across the records.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Immediacy in Recording
notes.originalTitle: Immediacy in Recording
notes.text:
Lofi explores why demos, rough takes and home recordings can feel more compelling than polished versions. The subject is the emotional force of a moment caught before it has been refined away.

Cindy Lee's Diamond Jubilee and a fragile Jackson C. Frank recording help frame the show. The original follows that idea through garage rock, folk and other recordings, with notes on the sound and feeling of each selection.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Reflections on Tonight’s Show: A Sonic Odyssey
notes.originalTitle: Reflections on Tonight’s Show: A Sonic Odyssey
notes.text:
The first Substack radio recap introduces writing as a companion to the weekly show. Lofi describes finding unexpected connections between records and using the blog to reflect on them afterward.

A visit to Surface Noise Records in Louisville and a newly discovered gospel compilation shape this set. The original includes individual notes on a program moving through gospel, soul, folk and jazz, from Abner Jay to Alice Coltrane.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Musical Reflections & Ramblings
notes.originalTitle: Musical Reflections & Ramblings
notes.subtitle: Reflections on Three Nights with the Sun Ra Arkestra
notes.text:
An opening statement for the blog is followed by a detailed recollection of three Sun Ra Arkestra performances at Portland's Hollywood Theatre in November 2024. Lofi describes each night differently: concentrated and joyful, unsettled and challenging, then searching before finding a collective direction.

The essay reflects on how a listener's own state affects a performance, and on the gratitude and connection that live improvisation can create.
notes.author: DJ Lofi / Jason Bimberg

notes.title: Coming soon
notes.originalTitle: Coming soon
